on 8 May, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1313 of 2014
Judgement:
The appellants are the petitioners in M.V.O.P.No.105 of 2006 on the file of the Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal-cum-VII Additional District Judge, Kakinada and the respondents are the
respondents in the said case.
2.

For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.
3.

The claimants filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents by praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- towards compensation for the death of deceased Potturi Veera Venkata Siva Ramakrishna Kiran Raju in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 26.12.2005.

entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text:
4. The brief averments of the petition are as follows:
The deceased was an employee in Andhra Pradesh Police Department working as Home Guard.

On 26.12.2005 at about VGKR, J 9.30 p.m. when the deceased along with his friend Pittala Vijaya Kumar were on duty as police home guard, while going on a motor cycle bearing No.AP 24K 2474 being driven by the deceased/ Potturi Veera Venkata Siva Ramakrishna Kiran Raju proceeding from Mummidivaram to Kakinada and when they reached Andhra Polytechnic college, Jagannadhapuram,
Kakinada, the driver of lorry bearing No.ADW 1388 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without blowing horn, dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, resulting which the deceased and pillion rider sustained injuries and the lorry ran over the body of the deceased and caused instantaneous death.

entities.text: Veera Venkata Siva Ramakrishna Kiran Raju
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: 5. The first and second respondents remained exparte.

The third respondent filed counter by denying the claim application and contended that the claimants are not entitled any compensation and the third respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
VGKR, J i.
Whether the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of lorry bearing No.ADW 1388 of 1st respondent?

7. During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners,
PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A7 were marked.
On behalf of 3rd respondent RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 and Ex.B2 were marked.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,82,000/- to the claimants towards compensation.
Being VGKR, J aggrieved by the impugned award, the petitioners filed the present appeal for enhancement of compensation.

9. Heard learned counsels for both the parties.
10.

Now, the point for consideration is:
Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
11. POINT:-
In order to prove the case of the petitioners, the first petitioner himself got examined as PW1.
PW1 is not an eye- witness.
The claim petitioners got examined the eye-witness as PW2.

The evidence of PW2 clearly shows that because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of crime vehicle only, the accident was occurred and the petitioners also relied on Ex.A1 attested copy of First Information Report and Ex.A5 attested copy of charge sheet.

The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.A1 and Ex.A5 clearly proves about the rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry bearing No.ADW 1388 and due to his rashness and negligence only, the accident was occurred and the deceased, who was riding the motor cycle, sustained severe injuries and VGKR, J died on the spot itself.
Therefore, in view of the above reasons, because of the rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry only, the accident was occurred.
The Tribunal also gave the same finding.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the learned Tribunal.
12. The petitioners in this case are claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the death of deceased in a road accident.

It is the contention of the petitioners that the deceased was working as Home Guard by the date of accident and drawing monthly Potturi Veera Venkata Satyanarayana ... vs N V Ramana 2 Others on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125237669/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: salary of Rs.5,000/- per month by the date of his death.
But the petitioners have not filed any salary certificate to prove the same.
The learned Tribunal by giving cogent reasons fixed an amount of Rs.3,000/- per month towards the monthly income of deceased.
The learned Tribunal deducted 1/3 of the said amount towards personal expenses of the deceased.

After deducting 1/3 amount, Rs.2,000/- per month is available to the dependents of the deceased, it come to Rs.24,000/- per annum and the multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is '15' and it comes to Rs.3,60,000/- (Rs.24,000 x 15 =
Rs.3,60,000/-).
Accordingly, VGKR, J the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,60,000/- to the petitioners towards loss of dependency.
In addition to that, the learned Tribunal also granted an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards love and affection, Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate.
Accordingly, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,82,000/- towards total compensation and the learned Tribunal rightly granted the said amount.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

13. The contention of the Insurance Company in the present appeal is, the date of accident is 26.12.2005 and the licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was expired by 20.11.2005 and subsequently it was renewed on 15.05.2006 and the same is proved by the Insurance Company.
Basing on the evidence produced by both the parties, the learned Tribunal came to conclusion that respondent No.3/Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

The material on record clearly goes to show that by the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle is not having driving licence and his driving licence is VGKR, J expired by the date of accident.
Originally he was having driving licence prior to the date of accident, but his driving licence was expired by the date of accident.

It was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Swaran Singh and others1:
The breach of policy condition, e.g,, disqualification of driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of section 149, have to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.
Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Swaran Singh and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
To avoid its liability towards insured,
the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

The learned counsel for claimants relied on a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Francisca Luiza Rocha and others Vs. K.Valarmathi and others2 in that decision it was held:
2004(2) ALD 36 2018 ACJ 1430 VGKR, J "Insofar as the second issue is concerned,
what we find from the materials on record is that the driving licence of the driver of the offending truck had lost its validity two months prior to the date of the accident.

sentences.text: In the present case the owner of the vehicle did not contest the proceedings to prove and establish that in spite of best efforts the fact that the driver did not have a valid driving licence was not known to him.
What alone stood proved (by the Insurer) was that the driver of the vehicle did not have a valid driving licence on the date of the accident.

As the driver had a licence but validity of the same had expired, we are of the view that the conclusion of the High Court that the said fact, by itself, constitutes a fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance is not correct".
Here in the present case first and second respondents are remained exparte.
The crime vehicle is insured with third respondent by the second respondent and policy was also in force by the date of accident.
Therefore, the second respondent is liable to pay the claim amount.

Since the crime vehicle is insured with third respondent by second respondent and policy is also in force and in view of the above decisions of Apex Court, the 3rd respondent/ Insurance company is directed to pay the total claim of Rs.3,82,000/- to the claimants at first instance, later recover the same from respondent No.2 by filing Execution VGKR, J Petition without filing independent suit, since second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

14. In the result, this appeal is disposed of, by modifying the order dated 11.03.2010 passed in M.V.O.P.No.105 of 2006 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VII Additional District Court (FTC), Kakinada.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VII Additional District Court (FTC), Kakinada
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is held that the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,82,000/- with interest @7.5% p.a., from the date of petition, till the date of payment.

The 3rd respondent/ Insurance Company is directed to pay the claim amount, within one month from the date of this judgment, to the claimants at first instance and later recover the same from respondent No.2 by filing an Execution Petition and without filing any independent suit.
On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the same along with costs and accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
_ __ V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J Dated: 08.05.2023.
